---
title: "Explainers"
---

How each GDAL mechanism that wxylib ports works, in GDAL and in wxylib,
and how the two are checked against each other. Each has one figure, made
by the script beside it.

- [How the warper works](warper.md): chunks, source windows and kernel
  scale, and why they change the values a warp writes.
- [Resampling kernels](kernels.md): bilinear and cubic weights, how they
  stretch for a coarser target, edges, nodata and the arithmetic order
  that decides the last digit.
- [Curvilinear grids](geoloc.md): GDAL's geolocation-array transformer,
  the backmap and the search that turns a position back into a cell of a
  swath.
- [Values at points](points.md): gdallocationinfo's cell and
  InterpolateAtPoint's kernels, how they differ from a warp's, and reads
  planned so each chunk is fetched once.
- [Polygons to cells](rasterize.md): GDAL's rasterizer by cell centre and
  ALL_TOUCHED, what happens to a polygon before the burn, and coverage
  fractions.
- [Overview selection](overviews.md): gdalwarp's `-ovr AUTO` rule for
  which resolution level a warp reads, checked against gdalwarp itself.
- [Multidimensional VRT views](mdim-vrt.md): which sources GDAL opens
  on a read of an `mdim.vrt`, why a missing `SourceSlab` count makes a
  one-day read open the whole series, and the rule and check for
  producers.
- [COG tiles as Zarr chunks](cog-tiles.md): the two steps that turn a
  COG tile's bytes into values (ZSTD and the TIFF horizontal predictor),
  how each view of a byte table names them, and who can decode each.
- [What the tests check](testing.qmd): GDAL as the oracle, and the bar of
  identity.
